sections.title: What Votalo is
sections.body: Votalo is an open-source project (MIT license) made by Votalo contributors. Today it runs as a test version, on the Monad test network.

sections.title: What data we handle
sections.body: We don't ask for a name, email, phone number or password. Here is what exists. On your device: your passkey's identifier and public data about your groups (identifiers, your member address in each group and your votes), kept in your browser's storage, plus your language and theme. Your fingerprint and your private key never leave your device. When you vote or create something: your member address in that group, the text you write (group name, question and options) and your vote are recorded on Monad. When you use the site: like any website, our hosting provider and the service that sends your action to the network can see your IP address and technical details of the connection.

sections.title: Cookies and tracking
sections.body: We don't use advertising or tracking cookies, or analytics tools. We store your language in a cookie and your theme (light or dark) in the browser, only so the site looks the way you left it.

sections.title: What we use the data for
sections.body: To make the service work: record your vote, show results and lists, and limit abusive use (for example, with limits per IP address).

sections.title: What is public and permanent
sections.body: What is recorded on Monad is public and can't be erased or changed, not even at the request of whoever wrote it. Think before writing personal details in a group name, a question or an option. Your votes appear under your credential in that group and the record is public: it is not a secret ballot.

sections.title: Who it is shared with
sections.body: With technical providers that make the service possible: our hosting provider, the Monad network, which is public, and an indexing service that reads the network to show lists and results. We don't sell data.

sections.title: Your options
sections.body: You can delete the data your browser keeps by clearing the site's data. What is recorded on Monad can't be deleted. For questions about this, use the contact below.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: If this changes, we'll update this page and its date.

sections.title: This is a test version
sections.body: Votalo runs on the Monad test network. It may change, restart or stop working without notice. Don't use it for decisions that need legal guarantees.

sections.title: Use it in good faith
sections.body: Use it in good faith. Don't use it to harass, deceive, or publish content that is illegal or harms other people. What you write is public and permanent, as the privacy notice explains.

sections.title: Your passkey
sections.body: Your passkey lives on your device or in your password manager. You're responsible for looking after it. If you lose it and it wasn't synced, we can't recover it or your credentials.

sections.title: Limits of the count
sections.body: Each credential votes once per vote. But Votalo doesn't verify who you are in real life: in open groups, a person with several passkeys could get in more than once, and an invite works for whoever uses it first. Results reflect what was recorded, not a verified identity.

sections.title: No warranty
sections.body: Votalo is provided as is, without warranties of any kind. To the extent the law allows, the people who contribute to the project are not liable for damages arising from its use.

sections.title: Open source
sections.body: The code is under the MIT license. You can review and reuse it under that license.

sections.title: Changes
sections.body: We may update these terms. The current version is the one on this page, with its date.

create.title: Create and share
create.body: Name your group, write the question and send the link on WhatsApp or Telegram.

vote.title: Everyone votes with their fingerprint
vote.body: When they open the link, each person confirms with Face ID, a fingerprint or their phone's PIN. Nothing to install.

results.title: Live results
results.body: Every vote counts once and stays in plain sight. No one can erase or change it.

Credentials.title: One fingerprint, many identities
Credentials.body: Your fingerprint creates a different credential in every group. Inside a group it's always you, so you count one vote. Between groups, no one can tell you're the same person.
Credentials.hint: Tap a group to see its credential.

stable.title: Stable inside the group
stable.body: Same fingerprint, same group: always the same credential. That's how one person gets one vote.

different.title: Different in every group
different.body: The credential in one group looks nothing like the one in another.

unlinkable.title: Impossible to link
unlinkable.body: No one can prove two credentials come from the same fingerprint.

Privacy.title: Privacy, no fine print
Privacy.lead: Votalo isn't a secret ballot box. It's a vote in plain sight of the group, with identities that don't reveal who you are outside it.

visible.title: Votes are visible inside the group
visible.body: Each vote appears under that person's credential in that group, and the record is public. It is not a secret ballot: that's how anyone can check the count is clean.

noPersonal.title: We don't ask for your details
noPersonal.body: No name, email or phone number. Your fingerprint stays on your device and never reaches us.

unlinked.title: Your groups can't be linked
unlinked.body: Someone who sees your credential in one group can't tell which other groups you're in.

ip.title: What the service does see
ip.body: The service that saves your vote can see your connection's IP address, like any website. It never sees your fingerprint or your keys.

Proof.title: Check it yourself
Proof.lead: You don't have to take our word for it. Everything can be checked.

contract.title: Verified contract
contract.body: The code that counts the votes is published and verified on Monad. You can read exactly what runs.

code.title: Open source
code.body: The whole app is public under the MIT license. Anyone can review, copy or improve it.

stats.body: Read straight from public records, untouched. Until there is data you'll see a dash.

secret.a: No. Each vote is visible inside the group under the credential of whoever cast it, and the record is public, so anyone who looks can see it too. Your name doesn't appear, but anyone who knows which credential is yours knows how you voted. If you need a secret ballot, Votalo isn't the right tool.

devices.q: Does it work on my phone?
devices.a: It depends. It works on iPhone with iOS 18 or newer (Safari or Chrome), on Android with Chrome, and on desktop Chrome if you save the passkey in the Google Password Manager or 1Password. Also on Windows 11 25H2 or newer. It doesn't work with the desktop Chrome local profile, Bitwarden or Dashlane.

unsupported.q: What if my browser doesn't allow it?
unsupported.a: Open the same link on a supported phone. When something doesn't work we show you a QR code so you can do it in a moment.

twice.a: Not with the same passkey: each credential votes once per vote. But in open groups, a determined person could create several passkeys and join more than once. In invite-only groups each invite is used once, which limits it to one entry per invite.

invite.q: Who can use an invite link?
invite.a: Whoever uses it first. An invite isn't tied to a specific person, so if the link reaches someone else, they can get in before the person you meant to invite. Share it only with the person you want to let in.

where.a: On Monad, a public network. That's why no one, not even us, can erase or change a result.

cost.q: Does it cost anything? Is this the final version?
cost.a: Voting costs you nothing: Votalo covers the technical cost. But today this is a test version, running on the Monad test network. Don't use it for decisions that need legal guarantees.

lost.q: What if I lose my phone?
lost.a: Your passkey lives in your password manager (iCloud, Google, 1Password). If you recover your account there, you recover your credential in every group. If it wasn't synced, there's no way to get it back.

passkey.a: It's the modern way to sign in without a password: your phone keeps a key and you unlock it with Face ID, your fingerprint or the PIN. No one else has it and it doesn't leave your device. Votalo uses it to create a different credential in every group.

final.a: No. Each person votes once per vote and the vote is final, so the result can be trusted.

create.a: Anyone who is part of the group. When you create a vote you choose the question, 2 to 6 options and how long it stays open.

report.q: How do I report a problem?
report.a: Open a report in the GitHub repository. It's public, so don't include personal details.

About.title: About Votalo
About.lead: Votalo lets any group decide together from a link, with each person's fingerprint.

what.title: What it does
what.body: Someone creates a group and a vote and shares the link on WhatsApp or Telegram. Each person votes from their phone with Face ID, their fingerprint or their PIN. No accounts, no passwords, nothing to install.

identity.title: A different identity in every group
identity.body: Your passkey, which lives on your phone or in your password manager, produces a different credential for every group. Inside a group your credential is stable and verifiable: one person, one vote per vote. Between groups there's no way to link them.

monad.title: Votes live on Monad
monad.body: Every action is recorded on Monad, a public network. That's why results are live and no one can erase or change them. Today Votalo runs on the Monad test network: this is a test version.

items.secret: It's not a secret ballot: each vote appears under the credential of whoever cast it, and the record is public.
items.passkeys: In open groups, a determined person could create several passkeys and get in more than once.
items.invite: An invite works for whoever uses it first. It isn't tied to a specific person.
items.late: In open groups, someone who joins later can still vote on votes that were already open.
items.ip: The service that saves your vote can see your connection's IP address, like any website.

HowPage.title: From a link to a decision
HowPage.lead: Here's what happens, from the moment someone creates the group until the results close.

create.one: Choose whether the group is open or invite-only.
create.two: Write the question and 2 to 6 options.
create.three: Decide how long it stays open: from 1 hour to 7 days.

vote.one: Open the link on your phone.
vote.two: Create your passkey once, with Face ID, your fingerprint or your PIN.
vote.three: Pick an option and press and hold the circle to vote.

results.one: The count updates live for the whole group.
results.two: It's one vote per person per vote, and it's final.
results.three: When time is up, the vote closes and the result stays recorded.

entry.title: Open or invite-only
entry.lead: You decide how people get in when you create the group.

open.title: Open

open.note: A determined person could get in with several passkeys.

invite.title: Invite-only
invite.body: Whoever created the group generates invites. Each one is used once.
invite.note: An invite works for whoever uses it first, so share it only with the person you want to let in.

PrivacyPage.title: Privacy, no fine print
PrivacyPage.lead: Votalo isn't a secret ballot box. It's a vote in plain sight of the group, with identities that don't reveal who you are outside it. Here's what is visible and what isn't.

items.votes: Each vote is visible under the credential of whoever cast it: inside the group and, because the record is public, to anyone who looks.
items.counts: The count for each option is public and updates live.
items.public: That a credential exists, and which group it belongs to, is recorded on Monad, a public network.

items.details: Your name, email or phone number: we don't ask for them.
items.biometrics: Your fingerprint or Face ID: they never leave your device.
items.groups: Which other groups you're in: credentials from different groups can't be linked.

items.ip: Your connection's IP address, like any website, and technical details such as your browser. It's used to run the service and limit abuse.
items.never: The service never sees your fingerprint or your keys: it only receives what your phone already signed.

items.secret: It's not a secret ballot: anyone who checks the record can see which credential voted what, and anyone who knows which one is yours knows how you voted.
items.forever: What is recorded on Monad can't be erased or changed, not even at your request. Don't write personal details in a group name, a question or an option.
items.passkeys: In open groups, a determined person could get in with several passkeys.

ProofPage.title: Check it yourself
ProofPage.lead: You don't have to take our word for it. Everything can be checked, and here's how.

contract.title: The contract
contract.body: The code that counts the votes is published and verified on Monad: you can read exactly what runs.

code.title: The code
code.body: The app and the contract are public under the MIT license, and have automated tests. Anyone can review, copy or improve them.

steps.title: Verify a result yourself
steps.lead: Four steps, without asking us for permission.

items.one: Open the contract on MonadVision with the link above.
items.two: Look at the contract's events: each vote cast is recorded with the vote, the credential of who voted and their option.
items.three: Count the votes for each option in those events.
items.four: Compare with the count you see in Votalo: they have to match.
